title: Research: classify 240-port optimal punctures and certify the all-target threshold
body:
## Result and overlap

**Research note / scoped finite classification; no new κ.** In the 240-port `(p,k)=(6,4)` paired geometry, exactly four five-port deletion sets decode a specified retained target using arbitrary global proper stars and uniform overlap corrections. Every optimum isolates one of the target's three-coordinate stars. Symmetry extends this classification to every target: there are exactly 160 minimum-weight codewords.

The same exact certificate proves that algebraic decoding of **all** surviving targets requires at least **85 deletions**, and supplies an attaining information set of 155 ports with independently checked unit-vector decoders. No paid supplier, frame schedule, or restoration implementation is claimed.

Two concurrent contributions arrived during the experiment and are explicitly credited:

- [#732](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/732), Luke Mansoor, proves the general one-target threshold and corroborates the same rank/distance. Those are not claimed as new here. This package adds the complete `(6,4)` equality classification and all-target information set.
- [#725](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/725), Sagar Thakrar, classifies 67 optima in the smaller `(5,4)` geometry, 63 requiring off-target stars. Here there are only four optima, all target-local.
- [#669](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/669), Sam Sung, supplied the original global-star puncture question and the target-local attaining witness, following Joel Pulikkan's #231 and the icekylinx/eumemic paired-cube lineage.

No concurrent implementation or proof is imported. Only `research/global-star-punctures/` is added. Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Source heads and inspected-byte SHA-256 pins are in `SOURCES.json`.

## Reproduce and validation

```sh
python3 -I -B research/global-star-punctures/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/global-star-punctures/test_verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_GLOBAL_STAR_PUNCTURES ports=240 rank=155 dual=85 minimum_deletions=5 optimal_sets=4 all_target_deletions=85 triples=2246839 controls=8 restored_ports=20 kappa=unchanged`, followed by five passing test groups.

- The certificate checks all 232 proper stars, three correction classes, independent primal/dual ranks, and an explicit 155-port information set.
- Complete enumeration of 28,681 short syndromes and 2,246,839 triples gives 40 hits and four distinct optimal supports. This is exhaustive finite coverage, with no heuristic or solver-status assumption.
- Independent ternary-word generation and direct decoder equations check all optima, 20 one-port restorations, 20 wrong five-port patterns, all 155 information-set decoders, scope controls, and optimized rejection of corrupted certificates.
- Python 3.9.6 and 3.12.14 pass, including isolated optimized mode. Regeneration is byte-identical across both. A committed-files-only relocated replay passes.
- Selected-record/source integrity and staged whitespace checks pass. The broad `make verify` attempt on unchanged base code stops at the copied-reversed producer: first on Python 3.9's missing `int.bit_count`, then with Python 3.12 on the local C++ toolchain's missing `<algorithm>` header. No full-suite or remote CI pass is claimed.

This is a finite scalar-code result, not a formal multiplication proof. Higher-degree totals, source-dependent corrections, other geometries, and physical/paid realization remain outside scope. Accepted conditional κ remains `51110230636731/31250000000000000`; inherited compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic obligations remain.

OS-random seed **42**, structural decoder track. No pinned coordination issue existed, so the claim is local. The final overlap refinement is recorded in `CLAIM.json`. Prepared by **Alishan Ladhani (@aladh)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, under Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed.

Publication refresh: 562 open PRs through #743; #725 and #732 remain at the credited heads, and main remains the exact base. The later arrivals add no matching `(6,4)` equality classification or all-target information set.
